heroHeadline: Opposition Leader Giorgi Baramidze Arrested for 'Treason' as Tbilisi Protesters Announce a United Opposition Front on Day 654
heroSubtitle: Georgia's Prosecutor General's Office arrested Giorgi Baramidze -- a former interior and defense minister and senior United National Movement figure -- on Sept. 11 on treason and sabotage charges tied to a July interview about the 1992-93 Abkhazia war, a case rights groups call the crackdown's furthest reach yet into named opposition leadership. Three days earlier, a bloc of 34 countries, including every EU member state, the UK, Ukraine, Canada, Australia and New Zealand, told the UN Human Rights Council in Geneva that Georgia's human rights situation continues to deteriorate and demanded the release of arbitrarily detained government critics. At the Sept. 12 Saturday march marking the movement's 654th consecutive day, civil society figures announced a push to unite all opposition and civic groups into a single coalition against Bidzina Ivanishvili's government. Separately, pardoned Russian activist Denis Kulanin left Georgia for a third country on Sept. 6 under a five-year re-entry ban, and animal-rights campaigner Tamaz Elizbarashvili began a hunger strike in pretrial detention on Sept. 8.
